title: Kauri: Old Kauri You Can Visit
meta_description: A kauri sheds its lower branches and bark, so what you meet is a bare grey column. Tāne Mahuta in the Waipoua Forest is 45 metres of it.
intro: A kauri does not look like other big trees, because it throws away the parts that would make it look like one. It sheds its lower branches as it grows and flakes off its lower bark in plates, which keeps climbers and epiphytes off the trunk, so what you walk up to is a bare grey column with the crown a long way overhead. Tāne Mahuta in the Waipoua Forest is 45 metres tall and most of that is column. Te Matua Ngahere, in the same forest, went the other way: shorter, squatter, and thicker round than anything else standing in New Zealand. Both are protected from their visitors as much as for them, because kauri dieback travels on the mud in a shoe tread. On the Coromandel, loggers left the Square Kauri standing because its angular trunk was the wrong shape to mill.
